newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Deal drives Anaconda shares to highs.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Deal drives Anaconda shares to highs.

text.p: Shares in nickel explorer Anaconda Nickel NL sprinted 32 cents to a record high of A$3.10 in morning trade on Wednesday, spurred on by settlement of legal action with Central Bore Nickel NL.

Brokers said buyers were out in force, buoyed by removal of uncertainty from the legal action launched by mining identity and Central Bore shareholder, Peter Salter, and then taken up by Central Bore itself.
"It's on the back of the legal settlement with very few sellers about," said broker Dirk Van Der Struyf of Hartley Poynton.
"The legal action looks to be over and people will now wait to watch developments."

The settlement sees Anaconda pay Central Bore a total of A$24.25 million, part of which is payable under an existing option, spread over three payments and conditional on the Murrin Murrin project proceeding and the price of copper exceeding US$3.50 per pound.
The settlement failed to have the same uplifting effect on Central Bore whose shares were 21 percent lower at 3.7 cents on heavy turnover of 14.89 million shares by 1.00 p.m. (0300 GMT).
"Central Bore has been sold down. Their shares were pumped up on hopes of a possibly better deal," Van Der Struyf said.
The Murrin Murrin project is forecast to produce 100 million pounds of nickel per year once fully operational in mid-1998.
By 1.00 p.m. (0300 GMT), Anaconda shares were 33 cents up at its record high of A$3.10 on turnover of 778,080 shares.
